## Verdict: request changes

42 findings across 19 files. One methodological caveat up front that shapes everything below: **`churn`, `blast_radius`, `blast_radius_importers`, and `recency` are 0 on all 42 findings** — an empty baseline means no git history and the import graph is effectively flat in this fixture. So the ranking signal here is `severity` × `confidence` × `agent_risk` only. I'm not treating a 0 blast radius as "this is isolated"; I'm treating it as "unmeasured."

I read the flagged sources rather than trusting summaries alone (`src/api/state.ts`, `src/api/files.ts`, `src/billing.ts` head), which changed my call on three findings noted below.

---

## Block merge — 9

| ID | Charge | sev | agent_risk | Why block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00006 | Contract Split-Brain (`Invoice`) | 0.96 | 0.40 | Highest severity in the report. `src/api/state.ts` declares 2 fields; `src/billing.ts` declares 11 — the absent 6 include `subtotalCents`, `taxCents`, `discountCents`, `currency`, `userId`. Two disagreeing money contracts with nothing in the build reconciling them. Confirmed by reading both files. |
| 00005 | Contract Split-Brain (`User`) | 0.90 | 0.40 | Same defect class, same pair of files, `createdAt` present on one side only. Fix as one change with 00006. |
| 00019 | Localhost-on-Disk | 0.60 | 0.30 | `SCHEMA_PATH = "/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json"` — the scan is literally reporting my own homedir baked into source. Works on exactly one machine; every CI runner and every other dev gets a silent `null` from `loadPlanSchema()`. **Score understates this** — medium severity, but it's a guaranteed breakage, not a risk. |
| 00018 | Dev-Server URL | 0.60 | 0.30 | `http://localhost:3000/admin` returned from `adminUrl()`. Same class as 00019: no environment other than a running local dev server works. Quick fix, no reason to defer. |
| 00012 | Half-UTC, Half-Local | 0.80 | 0.36 | Single receiver `d` mixes `getUTCFullYear()` and `getMonth()`. Fails silently by the host's UTC offset — the worst failure mode there is, because it passes in one timezone and corrupts in another. |
| 00001 | Temporal Recklessness (`date.ts`) | 0.80 | **0.44** | Highest `agent_risk` in the entire report. 8 clock reads across the module means nothing in `date.ts` is pinnable in a test — which is why 00012/00014/00020 could land undetected. Fixing this first is what makes the rest of the date cluster verifiable. |
| 00007 | God Function (`generateInvoice`) | 0.90 | 0.38 | 204 lines, 3.4× threshold, mixing pricing / discounts / tax / persistence / audit / email / retry. Normally I'd warn on a large function, but this PR *introduces* it against an empty baseline — there's no "pre-existing, refactor later" defence. `effort: small` and the file's own comment concedes there are no seams. |
| 00017 | False Identity (`calculateRefundPreview`) | 0.55 | 0.31 | Only medium severity, but the highest-consequence agent trap in the PR: a `calculate*`-prefixed function that awaits `saveRefundAudit` **and `sendRefundEmail`**. Any agent — or human — will treat it as pure and call it speculatively, and customers get refund emails. Rename is a one-liner. |
| 00039 | Catch and Release | 0.35 | 0.16 | **I'm overriding the score here.** It scores low on both axes, but this is a bare `catch {}` in `generateInvoice` whose own comment admits "caller has no way to know the email failed" — no binding, no log, no telemetry, in the money path. Silent failure in billing is an incident generator regardless of what the ladder says. One-line fix. |

The date-correctness findings (00001, 00012, plus 00014/00020 below) are one work item, not four — fix the clock injection and the UTC/local split together.

## Warn — 20

Land these as follow-ups; none justify holding the PR on its own.

**Highest agent risk in this bucket** (these mislead agents more than they break runtime):
- **00003** Missing Agent Context — sev 0.60 / ar **0.42**. No `AGENTS.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no skills, and `package.json` declares a `bin` (`messy`) nobody can discover. Cheap, high leverage.
- **00004** String Sprinkles (`"enterprise"`) — 0.50 / **0.42**. Four production files across four areas. This is duplicated policy in waiting.
- **00002** Return Shape Roulette — 0.30 / **0.43**. Low severity, top-quartile agent risk: three return shapes with 0% key overlap and no annotation. Classic case where agent_risk earns its place as a separate axis.
- **00008** Duplicated Navigation Source — 0.60 / 0.38 · **00009** Route Metadata Drift — 0.60 / 0.38. `/settings/billing` is called Plans, Billing, *and* Subscription across five places. Fix together; 00009 subsumes 00008.
- **00010** Sync I/O in Hot Path — 0.40 / 0.38 · **00011** Option Bag Junk Drawer — 0.30 / 0.38 · **00013** Negative Flag Maze — 0.25 / 0.36 (`!disableBilling && !skipRetry` — cheap to invert, and inverted-flag edits are a common agent failure).
- **00015** Temporal Recklessness (`billing.ts`) — 0.60 / 0.34 · **00014** Timezone Roulette — 0.60 / 0.35 · **00020** DST-Naive Day Math — 0.60 / 0.30. Same work item as the blocking date cluster; folding them in is nearly free.
- **00016** Unfinished Business (`todo.ts`) — 0.40 / 0.32. 424 markers per 1k LOC is absurd, but it's an isolated 33-line file.
- **00021** Concept Alias Drift — 0.55 / 0.30. account/organisation/team/workspace all naming one concept across 5 files.
- **00022** Logic in the Alibi — 0.50 / 0.30. "Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves" sits directly above `calculateRefundPreview`, which enforces none of it. Related to 00017; worth resolving in the same pass.
- **00023** Commented-Out Corpse — 0.45 / 0.29 · **00027** Test That Proves Nothing (0 asserts) — 0.45 / 0.27 · **00036** weak matcher — 0.25 / 0.23. The two test findings mean `billing.test.ts` protects nothing; 00027 is the more serious of the pair.
- **00037** God File — 0.60 / 0.18. 310 lines vs a 300 threshold — 1.0×, barely over. Resolves itself if 00007 is fixed.
- **00034** SVG With Embedded Raster — **sev 0.75** / ar 0.24. The clearest severity/agent-risk divergence in the report: high severity, but it's an asset-pipeline defect that no agent will reason wrongly about. Exactly why I'm not blocking on severity alone.
- **00040** Phantom Accomplice — 0.25 / 0.16, conf 0.56. Low-confidence, test-only — but `package.json` has **no dependencies block at all** while `billing.test.ts` imports `vitest`. A clean install genuinely can't run the tests. Worth more than its score.

## Ignore — 13

Naming taste, low-confidence heuristics, and asset nits. All ≤0.40 severity with ≤0.30 agent_risk, no correctness consequence.

- **00024, 00030** Unprefixed Boolean (`paid`/`expired`/`stale`, `disableBilling`/`skipRetry`) — 0.30 / 0.29, 0.26. House-style preference.
- **00026** Plural Mismatch — 0.30 / 0.28. Detector self-declares "v1 — type aliases and generics silently skipped."
- **00025** Temporal Recklessness (1 use in `state.ts`) — 0.35 / 0.28. One `Date.now()` in a module-level const.
- **00028** Date String Sewing — 0.30 / 0.26 · **00029** Host-Locale Drift — 0.30 / 0.26. Real but marginal; they'll get swept up if the date cluster is done properly.
- **00031, 00032, 00033** Orphaned Destination ×3 — 0.40 / 0.26, **conf 0.65** (lowest in the report). "Unreachable" on a brand-new PR usually means "not wired up yet," which is expected, not a defect. Low confidence is doing correct work here.
- **00035** Docs-Code Drift — 0.35 / 0.24. One broken relative link.
- **00038** Icon-Sized Raster (32×32 PNG) — 0.35 / 0.16 · **00041** Oversized Raster (254 KB, threshold 200) — 0.40 / **0.14**. Perf budget items, 1.27× over threshold.
- **00042** Unfinished Business (`billing.ts`, 12.9/1k LOC vs threshold 10) — 0.20 / **0.08**, lowest aggregate in the report. Correctly ranked last.

---

**Two things worth flagging about the report itself**, since you're evaluating the scanner as much as the code:

1. The scoring got the *relative* order right but under-weights environment-portability findings. 00019 and 00018 score 0.30 agent_risk and sit at rank 19/18, yet they're the only two findings that break with certainty rather than probability. `hardcoded_local_path` with a real homedir in it arguably deserves a severity floor.
2. `severity` and `agent_risk` genuinely disagreed in both directions and both times the split was informative — 00034 (high sev, low agent risk → warn) and 00002 (low sev, high agent risk → warn, not ignore). That's the axis earning its keep.

This is the intentional-mess fixture, so "block merge" is the hypothetical the scenario asked for, not advice to change `examples/`.
